4GB/0-swap host is the root cause of gateway kills - swapfile still not applied
The 2026-08-28 8.5h gateway outage was host-level memory exhaustion (SIGKILL): 4GB RAM, zero swap, desktop stack + Chrome + kanban workers starved the box. Mitigations deployed 2026-08-29 (kanban.max_in_progress=3, chrome-idle-close, supervisor daemon) but the root fix remains unapplied: a 2-4GB swapfile. On a 4GB/0-swap host the kernel reaps a process when memory bottoms out - the supervisor can relaunch into a still-starved host, tripping the crash-loop guard. Recommend Josh/Winston add a swapfile (root fix) to eliminate the class of failure entirely.

Learnings integrity guard: 3 precision/scope defects found on its first day
The 2026-09-12 guard works (it caught the 7th catalogue corruption), but three defects surfaced the same day. (1) FALSE POSITIVE on content-preserving edits: cards/gmail.md had its labelIds trap reworded and moved to the end of the file - no content lost - and the guard reported "TRAP deleted" plus "UPDATE note deleted", because it compares exact strings (case-sensitive titles, exact Symptom text) against HEAD. (2) SCOPE: the guard is wired as a pre-commit gate that `exit 1`s ALL of nightly-backup.sh, so one false positive blocks committing every unrelated vault change for that night. (3) EXIT CODE: every path ends in sys.exit(0), so both the cron and the backup gate key off non-empty OUTPUT only - any future caller that checks the exit code will read corruption as success. Recommended: normalise trap titles (lowercase/trim) and treat a missing UPDATE note as satisfied when the same text appears anywhere in the file; scope the gate to the learnings paths (or warn-and-continue); return a non-zero exit on FAIL. NOT changed autonomously - the guard gates a production backup.

Chrome never starts for PandaDoc: the shell guard blocks each launch, so the CDP is always dead
Quote intake needs Chrome DevTools on port 9222, but every attempt to start Chrome this week was launched with an ampersand inside the foreground shell, so the guard refused it and Chrome never came up. The cost is 11 dead CDP probes between 5 and 10 September, each one burning a turn before extraction falls back to raw HTTP. scripts/ has chrome-idle-close.py to stop Chrome and nothing to start it, so the start sequence gets re-invented by hand every time. Fix: add scripts/chrome-cdp-up.sh that checks port 9222, launches Chrome with terminal(background=true) and no ampersand, then polls /json/version until ready. The existing pandadoc card blames the idle-close watchdog, which is wrong: this week Chrome was never launched at all.
